**No.** The story is almost entirely scene. It is a real-time dialogue with only brief stage directions ("Setzt sich", "Lange Pause. Draußen wird es dunkel"). There is virtually no summary or exposition. We never learn what happened between Jonas and Marek, why they drifted apart, what the broken step means, or how long it has been since they last met.

The subtext and fragments ("An der ich damals… egal", "Weiterfahren vor allem") hint at a shared history but never fill it in. This creates tension, but it leaves the reader without enough background to fully grasp the stakes. The piece therefore relies heavily on scene at the expense of exposition rather than balancing the two.
